subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
title: Prophets mentioned in the Qur’an
overview: Allah sent prophets to guide people, and the Qur’an names twenty-five of them. In this sub-strand you will learn those names, study their virtues of patience, honesty, truthfulness, generosity and obedience, and practise the same virtues in your own day.

lessons.title: Who the prophets are
objectives: State that belief in the prophets is a pillar of Iman.
Begin the list of the twenty-five prophets with the earliest names.
lessons.intro: Some learners in your class may be called Adam, Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa or Muhammad. Those names belong first to prophets of Allah. Believing in all of them is a pillar of Iman.
lessons.notes:
### What a prophet is
A prophet is a person chosen by Allah to receive His message and to guide people. A rasul, or messenger, is sent with a revealed law or book, or to a people. Every messenger is a prophet. Prophets are human beings. They eat, sleep and walk in the markets, and they do not lie or betray the message. They are the best of people, and they are protected from teaching falsehood about Allah.

### A pillar of Iman
Belief in the prophets is one of the pillars of Iman. A Muslim believes in all of them, from the first to the last. We do not accept some and reject others. The Qur’an praises those who say they make no distinction, in belief, between any of Allah’s messengers (Qur’an 2:285). Muhammad (S.A.W.) is the last of them, the seal of the prophets (Qur’an 33:40). No prophet comes after him.

### Names to start with
The Qur’an mentions twenty-five prophets by name in the passages Muslims use for this list, including Qur’an 4:163-165, 6:84-86 and 21:85-88, together with other verses that name Adam, Hud, Salih and Shuayb. The earliest in the list you will memorise are Adam, Idris, Nuh, Hud and Salih.

Adam (alayhis-salam) was the first human being and the first prophet. Nuh (alayhis-salam) called his people for a very long time. The Qur’an says he remained among them for a thousand years minus fifty years (Qur’an 29:14). Hud was sent to the people of Ad, and Salih was sent to the people of Thamud.

Look around the class. If a learner carries one of these names, that name is a reminder of a prophet, and it should be used with respect.

keyWords.meaning: a person chosen by Allah to guide people with His message
a prophet sent with Allah’s message to a people

examples.problem: A learner says, “I believe in Muhammad only, not in Musa or Isa.” Which pillar has he broken?
steps: Belief in all the prophets is a pillar of Iman.
The Qur’an forbids accepting some messengers and rejecting others.
Muhammad (S.A.W.) is the last, and the earlier prophets are also believed in.
examples.answer: He has left out part of the pillar of belief in the prophets. A Muslim believes in all of them.

activity.title: Names of prophets in our class
materials: A list of the first five names on the board
steps: With respect, identify learners who are named after prophets, such as Adam, Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa or Muhammad.
Write the five names Adam, Idris, Nuh, Hud and Salih in your notebook.
Beside each name that you already know, write one true fact from the lesson.
Say together: we believe in all the prophets, and Muhammad (S.A.W.) is the last.

practice.question: What is a prophet?
practice.answer: A person chosen by Allah to receive His message and guide people.

practice.question: Who is the last prophet?
practice.answer: Muhammad (S.A.W.), the seal of the prophets.

practice.question: Name the first five prophets in the list you are learning.
practice.answer: Adam, Idris, Nuh, Hud and Salih.

practice.question: How long does the Qur’an say Nuh remained among his people?
practice.answer: A thousand years minus fifty years.

summary: A prophet is a human being chosen by Allah to guide people.
Belief in all the prophets is a pillar of Iman.
Muhammad (S.A.W.) is the last prophet. The list begins Adam, Idris, Nuh, Hud and Salih.

lessons.title: From Ibrahim to Yusuf
objectives: Name the prophets from Ibrahim to Yusuf.
Keep the growing list in order.
Recall one sure fact about Ibrahim, Musa’s family line, or Yusuf without mixing up their stories.
lessons.intro: Ibrahim (alayhis-salam) is a father of prophets. From his family came messengers whose names you already hear in dua and in the Qur’an. This lesson adds them to the list of twenty-five.
lessons.notes:
### The next names
After Adam, Idris, Nuh, Hud and Salih, learn these prophets in order:

6. Ibrahim
7. Lut
8. Ismail
9. Ishaq
10. Yaqub
11. Yusuf

Ibrahim (alayhis-salam) called people to worship Allah alone and broke the habit of idol worship. He is called Khalilullah, the close friend of Allah. Lut (alayhis-salam) was sent to a people who rejected Allah’s limits. Ismail (alayhis-salam) and Ishaq (alayhis-salam) were sons of Ibrahim. Yaqub (alayhis-salam) was the son of Ishaq, and Yusuf (alayhis-salam) was the son of Yaqub.

### A fact you can be sure of
The Qur’an tells the story of Yusuf: his brothers wronged him, Allah raised him in Egypt, and he later forgave his brothers and provided for them. That story is a full surah, Surat Yusuf. You do not need every detail yet. You do need his name in the list, and the lesson that he remained truthful under hardship.

Qur’an 6:84-86 mentions Ibrahim’s descendants among the guided: Ishaq, Yaqub, and later Yusuf among other prophets. Write the eleven names you now have, from Adam to Yusuf, until you can say them without looking. The remaining fourteen come in the next lesson. Do not skip a name, because the outcome is to mention all twenty-five.

keyWords.meaning: the close friend of Allah, a title of Ibrahim (alayhis-salam)
peace be upon him; said after a prophet’s name

examples.problem: Put these six names in the order used in class: Yusuf, Ibrahim, Ismail, Lut, Yaqub, Ishaq.
steps: Ibrahim comes first among them.
Then Lut, then Ibrahim’s sons Ismail and Ishaq.
Then Yaqub, then Yusuf.
examples.answer: Ibrahim, Lut, Ismail, Ishaq, Yaqub, Yusuf.

activity.title: Write the prophets from Adam to Yusuf
materials: Name cards for the eleven prophets
steps: Arrange the cards from Adam to Yusuf.
Check the order with the verses your teacher points to in Qur’an 6:84-86 and with the class list.
Each learner writes the eleven names in the notebook.
Say the list aloud twice as a group.

practice.question: Who is called Khalilullah?
practice.answer: Ibrahim (alayhis-salam).

practice.question: Name the two sons of Ibrahim included in the list of prophets.
practice.answer: Ismail and Ishaq.

practice.question: Whose son was Yusuf?
practice.answer: Yusuf was the son of Yaqub.

practice.question: Recite the eleven names from Adam to Yusuf in order.
practice.answer: Adam, Idris, Nuh, Hud, Salih, Ibrahim, Lut, Ismail, Ishaq, Yaqub, Yusuf.

summary: Ibrahim, Lut, Ismail, Ishaq, Yaqub and Yusuf follow the first five prophets.
Ismail and Ishaq were sons of Ibrahim, Yaqub was the son of Ishaq, and Yusuf was the son of Yaqub.
The list from Adam to Yusuf has eleven names.

lessons.title: From Ayyub to Muhammad (S.A.W.)
objectives: Name the prophets from Ayyub to Muhammad (S.A.W.).
Acknowledge belief in every prophet, with Muhammad as the last.
lessons.intro: The second half of the list includes Musa, Dawud, Sulayman, Isa and Muhammad (S.A.W.). When these fourteen names join the first eleven, the twenty-five are complete.
lessons.notes:
### The remaining prophets
Continue the list in this order:

12. Ayyub
13. Shuayb
14. Musa
15. Harun
16. Dhul-Kifl
17. Dawud
18. Sulayman
19. Ilyas
20. Al-Yasa
21. Yunus
22. Zakariyya
23. Yahya
24. Isa
25. Muhammad (S.A.W.)

Musa (alayhis-salam) was sent to Fir’awn and was given the Tawrah. Allah spoke to him, as Qur’an 4:164 states. Harun was his brother and a prophet with him. Dawud was given the Zabur (Qur’an 4:163). Sulayman was the son of Dawud and a prophet-king. Yunus (alayhis-salam), also called Dhul-Nun, called on Allah from inside the fish. Zakariyya was the father of Yahya. Isa (alayhis-salam), the son of Maryam, is a prophet and messenger. He is not the son of Allah. Surat Al-Ikhlas has already taught that Allah does not beget.

Shuayb, Dhul-Kifl, Ilyas and Al-Yasa are also among the twenty-five. Do not drop their names because the stories are shorter in class.

### The full belief
Say the twenty-five names until they are firm. Believe in every one of them. Love them and follow the message as completed by Muhammad (S.A.W.). We say “alayhis-salam” after the earlier prophets and “Sallallahu alayhi wa sallam” after Muhammad. Rejecting Isa, or calling him God, both contradict this pillar. He is a honoured prophet of Allah, and Muhammad is the last messenger.

keyWords.meaning: may Allah send prayers and peace upon him; said after the name of Prophet Muhammad

examples.problem: A classmate says Isa is the son of Allah, and another says Isa was not a prophet. How does the list of twenty-five correct both sentences?
steps: Isa is prophet number 24 in the class list. He is a true prophet.
Allah has no children, as Surat Al-Ikhlas teaches.
Muhammad (S.A.W.) is the twenty-fifth and the last.
examples.answer: Isa is a prophet of Allah, not His son. We believe in him and in Muhammad (S.A.W.) as the final prophet.

activity.title: Write all twenty-five names
materials: The references Qur’an 4:163-165, 6:84-86 and 21:85-88 as the teacher reads the names
steps: Listen as the teacher reads the prophets named in those passages.
Write all twenty-five names in order in your notebook.
Cover the page and, in pairs, test each other on any five names.
End by stating that belief in all of them is a pillar of Iman and that Muhammad (S.A.W.) is the last.

practice.question: Who was given the Tawrah, and who was given the Zabur?
practice.answer: Musa was given the Tawrah, and Dawud was given the Zabur.

practice.question: Where does Isa stand in the list, and who comes after him?
practice.answer: Isa is the twenty-fourth. Muhammad (S.A.W.) is the twenty-fifth and the last.

practice.question: Name Dhul-Kifl’s place among these prophets: is he included in the twenty-five?
practice.answer: Yes. Dhul-Kifl is one of the twenty-five prophets.

practice.question: How many prophets are in the full list?
practice.answer: Twenty-five.

summary: The list ends with Ayyub, Shuayb, Musa, Harun, Dhul-Kifl, Dawud, Sulayman, Ilyas, Al-Yasa, Yunus, Zakariyya, Yahya, Isa and Muhammad (S.A.W.).
There are twenty-five prophets to mention.
We believe in all of them, and Muhammad (S.A.W.) is the seal of the prophets.

lessons.title: Patience and obedience of the prophets
objectives: Explain patience using the examples of Nuh and Ayyub.
Explain obedience using Ibrahim and Yunus.
Write the meaning of each virtue in a notebook sentence.
lessons.intro: The prophets were not guides only because of miracles. They were guides because of character. Two of their virtues are patience when the road is long, and obedience when the command is hard.
lessons.notes:
### Patience
Sabr means staying firm on what is right, without giving up and without complaining against Allah. Nuh (alayhis-salam) called his people to Allah for a thousand years minus fifty, and most of them still refused (Qur’an 29:14). He did not abandon the message. Ayyub (alayhis-salam) was tested with serious illness and loss. He called on his Lord and remained patient. The Qur’an says Allah answered him and removed the harm (Qur’an 21:83-84).

Patience is not silence in the face of bullying that you should report. It is firmness: you keep praying, you keep telling the truth, and you do not insult Allah because a week has been difficult.

### Obedience
The prophets obeyed Allah even when the command cost them comfort. Ibrahim (alayhis-salam) was tested with a command about his son. The son, understanding the dream his father had been shown, said that his father should do what he was commanded, and Allah ransomed the son with a great sacrifice (Qur’an 37:102-107). That obedience is remembered at Eid al-Adha.

Yunus (alayhis-salam) left his people without waiting as he should have. He was swallowed by the fish. Inside it he obeyed by turning back to Allah with the words: there is no god but You, glory be to You, I have been among the wrongdoers (Qur’an 21:87). Allah saved him. Obedience includes coming back as soon as you know you were wrong.

Write both virtues in your own words and attach one prophet to each, so the story and the virtue stay together.

keyWords.meaning: patience; remaining firm in obedience to Allah

examples.problem: A learner has invited a classmate to salah for many days and feels like stopping. Which prophet’s patience speaks to this moment?
steps: Nuh continued his call for a very long time.
The learner’s few days are small beside that patience.
He continues kindly, without insulting the classmate.
examples.answer: Nuh (alayhis-salam). The learner keeps inviting kindly and does not give up at once.

activity.title: Describe patience and obedience
materials: Verses read by the teacher: Qur’an 21:83-84, 21:87, 29:14 and 37:102-107
steps: In pairs, describe the patience of Nuh and of Ayyub in two or three sentences.
Describe the obedience of Ibrahim and his son, and the return of Yunus to Allah.
Write the points in your notebook under the headings Patience and Obedience.
Read one point to the class.

practice.question: How did Ayyub show patience?
practice.answer: He remained patient during serious illness and called on Allah, who removed the harm.

practice.question: What did Yunus say when he turned back to Allah from inside the fish?
practice.answer: There is no god but You. Glory be to You. Indeed, I have been among the wrongdoers.

practice.question: What virtue did Ibrahim and his son show when Ibrahim was tested?
practice.answer: Obedience. The son told his father to do what Allah had commanded.

summary: Nuh and Ayyub are models of patience.
Ibrahim and his son obeyed Allah in a hard test, and Yunus obeyed by turning back.
Patience and obedience are virtues for character, not only stories.

lessons.title: Honesty, truthfulness and generosity
objectives: Explain honesty and truthfulness from the lives of the prophets.
Explain generosity from Ibrahim and Muhammad (S.A.W.).
Separate a true virtue from a similar bad habit.
lessons.intro: People trusted the prophets with news from Allah because the prophets did not lie about small things. They also gave freely. Honesty, truthfulness and generosity are the next virtues to learn.
lessons.notes:
### Honesty and truthfulness
Honesty means dealing fairly: you do not steal, cheat in measure, or take a hidden advantage. Truthfulness means your words match the facts. All the prophets were truthful. Their people sometimes rejected the message, but they could not prove that the prophet was a liar in his character.

Muhammad (S.A.W.) was called As-Sadiq Al-Amin, the truthful and trustworthy, before prophethood. Yusuf (alayhis-salam) was trusted with the storehouses of Egypt because the king saw that he was knowledgeable and trustworthy. A prophet does not pass an exam by cheating or sell goods by hiding a fault.

### Generosity
Generosity is giving freely what is lawful to give. Ibrahim (alayhis-salam) hurried to prepare food when guests came to him (Qur’an 51:24-27). He did not wait to be pushed. Muhammad (S.A.W.) was the most generous of people, and he was even more generous in Ramadan (Bukhari). He did not love hoarding.

### Do not mix the virtue with a fault
Truthfulness is not the same as saying a hurtful thing for fun and then claiming “I was only honest”. Honesty does not cancel kindness. Generosity is not giving away someone else’s property, and it is not wasting. A generous learner shares a pencil, gives from what a parent allows, and still leaves enough for his or her own need. Write one clear sentence for each virtue so that you can use it in the role-play of the next lesson.

keyWords.meaning: dealing fairly and not taking what is not yours
giving freely from what is lawful

examples.problem: A seller of mangoes hides the rotten ones under the good ones. Which virtue of the prophets has he broken, and what would Yusuf’s example suggest?
steps: Hiding a fault in a sale is dishonest.
The prophets were trustworthy in their dealings.
He should show the fruit as it is or remove the rotten ones.
examples.answer: He has broken honesty. A prophetic example is to deal in a way people can trust.

activity.title: Three virtues on paper
steps: In small groups, discuss honesty, truthfulness and generosity using the prophets named in the lesson.
Write one sentence for each virtue and one prophet beside it.
Add one school example that is really the virtue, and reject one example that only pretends to be.
Read your sentences to another group.

practice.question: What titles did people give Muhammad (S.A.W.) that show truthfulness and trust?
practice.answer: As-Sadiq, the Truthful, and Al-Amin, the Trustworthy.

practice.question: How did Ibrahim show generosity to his guests?
practice.answer: He hurried to prepare food for them.

practice.question: Why is sharing another person’s pencil without permission not generosity?
practice.answer: Generosity gives what you may lawfully give. Taking someone else’s property is not giving.

summary: The prophets were honest and truthful, and people could trust their dealings.
Ibrahim fed his guests quickly, and Muhammad (S.A.W.) was most generous, especially in Ramadan.
Kind truthfulness and lawful giving are the real virtues.

lessons.title: Practising the virtues of the prophets
objectives: Role-play patience, honesty, truthfulness, generosity and obedience.
Choose one virtue to practise this week.
State again that belief in the prophets is a pillar of Iman.
lessons.intro: A virtue that stays inside a notebook has not yet formed character. The prophets’ patience, honesty, truthfulness, generosity and obedience are for the corridor, the market and the kitchen, not only for a test.
lessons.notes:
### From story to action
Apply each virtue in a way that fits your age:

- Patience: keep learning a surah that is taking time. Do not tear the page or insult yourself. Ask for help and continue, as Nuh continued and as Ayyub remained firm.
- Obedience: do the halal thing your parent or teacher asks when it does not contradict Allah. If you slipped, return quickly, as Yunus returned to Allah with dua.
- Honesty: give back extra change. Do not hide a fault in something you sell or swap.
- Truthfulness: tell the teacher what actually happened when a window breaks. As-Sadiq did not invent a story.
- Generosity: share food or a skill. Explain a sum to a classmate who is stuck.

### Belief that changes behaviour
Acknowledging the prophets as a pillar of Iman means you mention all twenty-five with respect, you refuse to mock any of them, and you try to wear their virtues. Saying “I believe in Musa” while cheating, or “I love Ibrahim” while refusing to share, leaves the belief unfinished. The pillar is in the heart, and the virtues show it in the limbs.

Choose one virtue for seven days. Tell a partner the exact action. At the end of the week, be honest about whether you did it. If you failed on one day, obey Allah by starting again the next morning. That second start is itself a prophetic lesson.

keyWords.meaning: to put a virtue into a real action

examples.problem: You accidentally break a friend’s ruler and feel like saying the desk broke it. Which virtue, and which prophetic title, correct you?
steps: Truthfulness means the words match the facts.
The Prophet (S.A.W.) was As-Sadiq.
You apologise and offer to replace the ruler if you can.
examples.answer: Truthfulness, following As-Sadiq. Admit the break and make it right.

activity.title: Role-play the five virtues
materials: Five situation cards: a hard surah, a parent’s lawful instruction, extra change, a broken ruler, a classmate without a pencil
steps: In groups, pick one card and act the wrong response, then the prophetic response.
The class names the virtue: patience, obedience, honesty, truthfulness or generosity.
Each learner writes the virtue he or she will practise this week and the exact action.
Close by reciting the number of prophets, twenty-five, and stating that belief in them is a pillar of Iman.

practice.question: Give one way to practise patience with schoolwork.
practice.answer: Keep learning a difficult surah or sum, ask for help, and do not give up in anger.

practice.question: Give one way to practise generosity without money.
practice.answer: Explain a lesson to a classmate or share time and learning materials.

practice.question: Why is mocking any prophet against this pillar?
practice.answer: Belief in all the prophets is a pillar of Iman, so every prophet is mentioned with respect.

practice.question: How many prophets must you be able to mention?
practice.answer: Twenty-five.

summary: Patience, obedience, honesty, truthfulness and generosity can be practised at school.
Belief in the prophets shows in respect for all twenty-five and in these virtues.
If you fail one day, start again the next day.

quiz.question: How many prophets are named in the list you learned?
quiz.explanation: The Grade 4 list has twenty-five prophets, ending with Muhammad (S.A.W.).

quiz.question: Who is the first prophet in the list, and who is the last?
quiz.explanation: Adam is the first human and the first prophet. Muhammad (S.A.W.) is the seal of the prophets.

quiz.question: Which statement about Isa (alayhis-salam) matches the pillar of Iman?
options: He is the son of Allah
He is a prophet of Allah, and Allah has no children
quiz.explanation: Isa is honoured as a prophet. Surat Al-Ikhlas teaches that Allah does not beget.

quiz.question: Who was given the Zabur?
quiz.explanation: Qur’an 4:163 says Dawud was given the Zabur.

quiz.question: Nuh’s long call to his people is an example of which virtue?
quiz.explanation: He remained among them for a thousand years minus fifty and did not abandon the message.

quiz.question: Ayyub (alayhis-salam) is remembered especially for patience during which test?
quiz.answer: Serious illness, after which he called on Allah and Allah removed the harm.

quiz.question: Ibrahim hurrying to feed his guests is an example of which virtue?
options: hiding a fault in a sale

quiz.question: Which action applies truthfulness at school?
options: Blaming the desk for something you broke
Telling the teacher what really happened
Copying and saying the work is yours
quiz.explanation: Truthfulness means your words match the facts, as in the title As-Sadiq.

quiz.question: What does Yunus turning to Allah from inside the fish teach?
options: that a sin cannot be followed by dua
that the fish was a prophet
that we may leave every duty
quiz.explanation: He admitted his fault and called on Allah, who saved him.

quiz.question: Belief in the prophets means…
quiz.answer: Believing in all twenty-five, respecting every one of them, and knowing that Muhammad (S.A.W.) is the last.
quiz.explanation: This belief is a pillar of Iman.

quiz.question: Which group is in the correct order?
quiz.explanation: After Ibrahim come Lut, then Ismail and Ishaq, then Yaqub, then Yusuf. The option that keeps Ibrahim before his descendants is correct.

sources: KICD Grade 4 Islamic Religious Education Curriculum Design (Revised 2024) — Strand 3.0 Pillars of Iman, Sub-strand 3.3 Prophets mentioned in the Qur’an
Sahih al-Bukhari: the Prophet (S.A.W.) was the most generous of people, and even more so in Ramadan
